# Contributor experience and UI direction

The design was reviewed with **Claude Opus 5.5**, requested and observed as `claude-opus-5-5`, with a successful consultation recorded at 2026-10-17T02:30:57.056827+00:00. The public record is [the sanitized UI concept](../planning/ui/ui-concept.json). Consultation advice was reconciled into the canonical plan; it does not create a competing backlog.

Editorial contribution ledger: calm dense data, clear typography, teal/slate/amber brand, generous navigation and evidence-first rows. Optional ASCII accent must not obscure data or imply unsupported 3D implementation.

## Essential behavior

- URL-persisted filters and explicit time bounds
- Evidence drawer with full-page equivalent
- Accepted and pending values visually and arithmetically separate
- Shared-rank ties and coverage-aware rank movement
- Directory includes attributable observed work, not only high-ranking accepted contributors
- Live updates held while reading; visible apply/pause control
- Accessible tables, sortable headers and mobile card parity
- Functional correction/opt-out destination with receipts

The organization overview gives equal access to contribution families. Boards use compact evidence-first rows, exact units and visible coverage, with mobile cards preserving the same information. Contributor portfolios show varied work without a universal score. An evidence drawer has a shareable full-page equivalent. A correction flow is only complete when submission reaches the authorized destination and returns a real receipt.

## Required states

- Loading
- Empty complete scope
- No filter matches
- Partial history
- Unsupported capability
- Pending evidence
- Stale data
- Disconnected collector
- Rebuilding snapshot
- Hidden/deleted contributor
- Source no longer public
- Corrected result

## Accessibility and live display

WCAG 2.2 AA target; keyboard, screen reader, contrast, zoom/reflow, reduced motion and live announcement testing; source/quality status always in words, not color alone.

Preserve keyboard focus, meaningful heading structure and screen-reader announcements. Status must have text as well as color. Real-time updates do not move rows beneath someone who is reading. The live wall includes a pause control, visible scope and freshness, reduced motion and a stale/disconnected state. Anonymous access must not require login; privileged controls belong in the authenticated console.

## Reconciled decisions

**Topic:** Tie ranking

**Master:** Dense ranks: 1, 2, 2, 3; deterministic ordering within ties has no credit effect.

**Consultant:** Competition ranks: 1, 2, 2, 4.

**Resolution:** Master dense-rank choice prevails; raw consultation remains historical advice.

**Topic:** Period presets

**Master:** Last 30 days by default; 7/30/90-day rolling, all-time, custom half-open UTC windows and calendar presets including quarter.

**Consultant:** Calendar quarter default; calendar month/year presets.

**Resolution:** Default follows the final master choice. Calendar presets remain supported without changing the 30-day default.

**Topic:** Canonical routes

**Master:** /leaderboards, /contributors, /contributions, /activity and /live.

**Consultant:** /boards, /people, /receipts and /wall.

**Resolution:** Final master route names prevail; equivalent UI journeys are mapped without duplicate endpoints.

**Topic:** Public actor wording

**Master:** User accounts, automation and all activity; a user-account event does not establish manual authorship.

**Consultant:** Humans and bots.

**Resolution:** Use master actor classes in UI filters and preserve declared assistance separately.

**Topic:** Repository and product name

**Master:** Proposed repository pick-your-ai-leaderboard; proposed product PickYour.AI Credits.

**Consultant:** Example repository credits.

**Resolution:** Repository name follows master; product name is a revisable design choice.

**Topic:** Number of issues

**Master:** 112 work packages under 20 epics and one program.

**Consultant:** 37 UI design sub-items in an independent outline.

**Resolution:** All UI items are traceability references to existing master packages; zero additional GitHub issues.

#### Scope rules

- Use stable IDs internally; names are display values and may change.
- Research T0-T6 is not the whole organization's program taxonomy.
- Website, Android and Apple programs may share a repository.
- A contribution may belong to multiple programs but counts once in an organization aggregate.
- Unknown or unassigned program remains visible without inferred membership.
- Invalid or incompatible filters get a visible explanation, not silent substitution.
- Default period is the last 30 days. Support 7/30/90-day rolling windows, all-time, custom half-open UTC windows and calendar presets including quarter.
- Public actor filters say user accounts, automation and all activity. An event attributed to a person account does not prove manual execution or absence of AI assistance.

### Screen behavior

**Overview:** Show all departments with the same visual weight and a clear explainable lead metric. Lead metrics prefer verifiable outcomes, but departments without an outcome metric show a clearly labeled observed measure or availability explanation. Never fabricate an accepted state to fill a slot. Keep the People link and unranked first-contribution strip visible. Unsupported departments remain discoverable.

**Board:** Header states measure, unit, period, date basis, actor scope, method version and coverage. Hold updates by default. Use a semantic table with contextual columns. An explicit contributor link opens a shareable proof drawer; a separate profile link remains a normal navigation target. Accepted and provisional values never share a rank numerator. Pending evidence is distinct from unsupported source capability, partial history, stale collection and unknown actor. None of those states is automatically a zero or an accepted outcome.

**Ties:** Use shared dense ranks 1, =2, =2, 3. Alphabetical/ID display within ties has no rank or credit effect. Top-N boundaries include tied contributors or provide explicit continuation. Small-cohort presentation and threshold are versioned policy choices; retain visible counts and do not invent inferior ranks.

**Loc:** Expose additions, deletions, net, changed files, PR count and PR-size context separately. Group source/docs/tests/generated/vendor/lockfile/other. Show bulk import, formatting and rename exclusions with exact classifier coverage. Do not use net LOC as a default merit ranking or code volume as the Overview lead.

**Profile:** Group measures by department, with no total score. Show evidence links, selected scope, verified roles, first observed contribution with coverage caveat and optional consented highlights. Distinguish no eligible activity from not measured. No public linking emails or inferred private work. Optional monthly summaries require complete enough data and an accessible table.

**Proof:** Show the exact observed action and actor role, activity/acceptance timestamps where applicable, current policy inclusion, public source, ingestion provenance, correction history and exclusion reason. GitHub author, merger, reviewer and closer are distinct roles. A missing actor does not become an assumed assignee.

**Methodology:** Each method contains what counts, unit, numerator/denominator, population, date basis, tie semantics, exclusions, sources, coverage, known gaps, gaming risks and policy version. Keep concise method disclosure on the board itself.

**Coverage:** Accessible repository/source/metric matrix and mobile per-repository list. Display history boundaries and outages, current freshness and attribution gaps. Avoid completeness percentages when the denominator is unknowable.

**Corrections:** Every proof offers a prefilled issue-form link for public factual corrections, with snapshot and receipt IDs. Sensitive privacy requests require a verified staffed private path before public launch; do not invent an email address or claim a nonfunctional form works. Later authenticated tools show preview, reason and reversible internal application.

### Design system

**Brand source sha:** c731bc451d227eac843750418b6de3c3377ea90b

#### Palette

**Lightbackground:** #f8fafc

**Darkbackground:** #020617

**Lightsurface:** #ffffff

**Darksurface:** #0f172a

**Brandteal:** #0f766e

**Darklinkteal:** #2dd4bf

**Changeaccent:** #fbbf24

**Typography:** Existing system sans for body and navigation; existing monospace with tabular numerals for metrics. Opus proposes Instrument Serif for page titles only; adopting it is optional and requires license verification, self-hosted subset, no-font fallback and a layout-shift check.

**Layout:** Hairline separators rather than a field of cards; 1280px default content max; spacing 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64; mobile starts at 320px reflow with 16px side padding; 640/1024/1280 layout changes.

**Density:** 44px comfortable row targets; compact mode only for fine pointers and sufficient viewport, retaining usable interactive targets.

**Drawer:** 480px supplementary panel on desktop, full-screen dialog below 1024px; focus placement, Escape, focus return and back navigation are defined.

#### Evidence labels

- Observed action
- Provisional or pending verification
- Qualified/accepted under a stated rule
- Reviewed manual recognition
- Excluded under stated policy
- Not measured, with source-specific reason

**Evidence glyphs:** Optional symbols accompany persistent text labels. No color-only or glyph-only meaning; no unsupported claim that glyphs alone guarantee accessibility.

**Ascii coordination:** Current #32/#33 proposals are unmerged and local-only. Reserve an optional empty decorative slot; do not create a dependency on their code. Any future artwork must be aria-hidden, bounded, pausable, responsive, reduced-motion aware and paused offscreen.

### Accessibility and resilience

- WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance target, measured contrast, keyboard support, semantic headings and tables, visible unobscured focus and skip navigation.
- Verify with keyboard and at least two representative screen readers; test 200% text/zoom, 400% reflow as appropriate and 320px CSS width.
- Use one polite live summary per applied batch. Do not announce each changed row or move focus automatically on background refresh.
- Tables retain captions, row/column headers and aria-sort; mobile stacked layouts preserve programmatic relationships.
- All charts have adjacent text/table equivalents; use explicit units and Intl formatting with visible UTC cutoff semantics.
- Support reduced motion, forced colors, no custom font, missing avatar, slow network, stale snapshot and failed refresh.
- Optional single-key shortcuts are discoverable and can be disabled; do not intercept text entry.
- Sanitize any rendered public source text, validate external source URLs, and export CSV safely against formula injection.
- Provide independent light/dark/system preference without requiring account creation or tracking.
- Synthetic fixtures are clearly named and carry a persistent banner on every route; they cannot silently enter public production datasets.
- Use precise user-account versus automation labels; keep execution mode and declared AI assistance as independent evidence fields, never infer them from a GitHub account type.

### Live display

**Read mode:** Hold while I read is default. Queue new snapshots and show an Apply updates control. Preserve filter state, scroll, selection and focus.

**Follow mode:** Explicit opt-in. No reordering while keyboard focus, pointer engagement or proof drawer is active. Apply coherent snapshots at safe intervals. No partial mix of policy/snapshot numerators and denominators.

**Freshness:** Show data-as-of timestamp, observation/ingestion freshness and reconciliation status distinctly. Labels are Fresh, Polling, Delayed, Reconciling, Stale or Error based on verified pipeline metadata, not a decorative always-green live indicator.

#### Wall modes

- Frozen snapshot
- Single board with safe auto-refresh
- Cycling live boards

#### Wall formats

- 16:9 at 1920x1080
- 16:9 at 3840x2160
- 9:16 portrait
- 4:3 optional

**Wall defaults:** 30-second cycle, minimum proposed 20 seconds, avatars off, safe margins, persistent scope and freshness, no marquee or count-up effects. Reduced motion uses instant transitions.

**Wall controls:** Pause/play, previous/next, cycle interval, display mode and motion setting. Configurator copies a public URL and never automatically launches OBS or external software.

**Fair exposure:** Cycle configured departments and tie continuation pages transparently. Offer an unranked contributor credits roll so high-volume contributors are not the only people ever displayed.

**Privacy:** Public eligible data only, no private Project metadata, no restricted evidence or identity emails. Respect contributor display suppression on every generated wall payload.
